images.title: Figs in boxes
images.purpose: Show that 12 figs can make a rectangle with several rows while 7 figs make only a single row.
images.composition: Two groups side by side with wide space between, 12 figs left and 7 figs right.
images.exact_structure: Left: exactly 12 equal teal #0072B2 round dots in a grid of 3 rows and 4 columns with equal gaps. Right: exactly 7 equal amber #E69F00 round dots in 1 row. A thin grey #6B7280 rectangle outline around each group. Exactly 2 groups, 19 dots.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a grid that is not exactly 3 by 4
images.takeaway: 12 figs form a 3 by 4 rectangle; 7 figs form only one row.
images.description: A teal grid of 12 dots in 3 rows of 4 beside an amber single row of 7 dots.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the rows and columns in each group and say how many figs there are.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture carries the main idea of this concept.
